title: How Cash on Delivery Works: COD Payments, Refunds and Settlement
summary: Understand how cash on delivery works for ecommerce, from payment collection and refunds to COD settlement timelines, fees, benefits and RTO controls.

### Key Takeaways


- Cash on Delivery (COD) allows customers to pay at delivery, while businesses bear the risk of RTO, delayed remittance and slower refund processes for customers who return their products.
- COD allows sellers to reach buyers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and newer audience segments, by providing them the convenience of paying at delivery. COD handling fees may apply; it does not guarantee lower prices or free shipping.
- COD refunds can be automated using payout links sent over WhatsApp or SMS, reducing manual data collection and errors in processing refunds. Customers must redeem the link, and bank processing can affect completion.


**Cash on Delivery (COD) payments** allow buyers to pay for items when they reach their doorstep rather than paying upfront at checkout online. Cash on delivery remains a major payment option in India, especially in Tier 2 and Tier 3 and when people are ordering from a website for the first time.


##


How Cash on Delivery Works: The COD Payment Process


1. Buyers confirm the way they want to pay on the checkout page by selecting cash on delivery (COD) over other[payment methods](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/payment-mode-types/) .
2. The store may then send them an OTP over WhatsApp or SMS to verify access to their mobile number and reduce the incidence of fake orders. OTP verification supports order confirmation, but does not guarantee buyer intent or prevent later cancellation.
3. You pack the order, generate the shipping label, and ship the item with a COD label through the ideal courier partner or shipping aggregator.
4. The delivery agent collects the amount quoted by the seller at the time of delivery through a UPI/QR, cash or card on delivery payment. If the buyer is not available at the location or their mobile remains unreachable, then a[Non-Delivery Report (NDR)](https://support.shiprocket.in/support/solutions/articles/43000664209-what-is-ndr-) is generated. The courier may reattempt delivery before the item moves back to the warehouse as a return to origin (RTO).
5. The courier or shipping aggregator then reconciles the payments from the buyers, deducts applicable shipping fees, and then makes the settlement to the seller’s account. Keep cash COD remittance separate from gateway settlement. RBI’s[Payment Aggregator Directions](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_ViewMasDirections.aspx?id=12896) , paragraph 18(b), prohibit using PA escrow accounts for cash-on-delivery transactions; this is not a blanket exemption from other laws.


##


COD Payments and Refunds: From Collection to Customer Credit


### Collecting Payment on Delivery


In ecommerce, “COD” often means pay on delivery, including physical cash. Some shipping partners also empower delivery agents with UPI codes and POS solutions that allow customers to pay through the following methods, where supported. RBI’s definition of cash-on-delivery specifically refers to banknotes or currency notes; digital doorstep payments use their respective payment rails.


- [UPI QR scan](https://www.cashfree.com/upi-qr-code/) (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm, etc.)
- Debit or credit cards (via supported courier devices)


### Handling COD Refunds


COD refunds can be a big operational bottleneck for both the seller and the shipping partner because the account information of the buyer may not be there on file. This becomes a problem when they return a delivered item, especially when there are strict deadlines in place for both returning the item as well as the refund process itself.


- **The Traditional Way:** Support teams will call customers and collect beneficiary details such as the name of the bank, the IFSC code and the account number before they process a refund, extending the refund timeline and potentially leading to errors in manual data collection. The delay depends on the seller’s process and the customer’s response.
- **The Automated Way with Cashfree:** Using **[Cashgram payout links](https://www.cashfree.com/cashgram/)** , businesses send out a payout link to the customer once the refund is approved. The customer simply clicks the link, completes verification, enters their UPI ID or bank details, and receives the refund after successful processing, reducing manual data collection errors.


Keep sufficient funds in your Payouts account and ask customers to[redeem their Cashgram](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payouts/cashgram/redeem-a-cashgram) before expiry. Instant transfers are supported, but pending, failed or reversed outcomes can occur. Track the final payout status before treating a refund as complete.

##


COD Benefits and Disadvantages for Ecommerce Businesses


### Benefits of Cash on Delivery


- **Higher Conversions & Trust:** Lowers friction at the buying stage, especially for buyers with low brand trust and who are from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
- **Wider Reach:** Has a wider reach as it lets buyers pay later at the time of receiving the product, at their own convenience, extending to people who are not comfortable with online transactions.
- **Lower Cart Abandonment:** It can reduce people dropping off when upfront online payment does not complete or when they prefer to pay later. Buyers still need funds at delivery.


### Disadvantages of Cash on Delivery


- High RTO Rates:[COD return to origin rates](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/cod-vs-prepaid-payments-solving-rto-challenges-for-ecommerce/) can be higher than for prepaid orders, depending on order quality, category and delivery experience. COD does not automatically include “try before you buy”. Sellers generally absorb the forward and return shipping costs in such cases.
- Delayed Cash Flow: Money can be tied up until the courier settlement cycle completes.
- Extra Fees & Cash Risks: Couriers may charge COD handling fees over the freight cost, which makes it inconvenient for the seller to plan ahead for the business, which could be a stumbling block, especially for early-stage startups.


##


COD Settlement: Remittance Timelines, Fees and Delays


Understanding when your money arrives is crucial for managing inventory and ad spend.


- **How Timelines Are Calculated:** COD settlement is usually counted from the **date of delivery (D)** , not the date the customer placed the order. Confirm the start date, working-day definition and payout schedule in your contract.
- **Standard Settlement Cycles:** Direct courier contracts and shipping aggregator plans have different cycles. Check your current account terms rather than assuming a universal timeline.
- **Early / Accelerated COD:** Many logistics aggregators offer faster remittance options, such as **D+1 or D+2** , depending on the provider and plan, either based on your account’s delivery track record or for an additional fee. Shiprocket describes Early COD as potentially available as soon as two days after delivery.
- **Where Cashfree Fits Into Settlement:** While your courier partner collects doorstep cash and handles COD remittance, **Cashfree** handles the digital side, settling upfront **Partial COD** deposits and **COD-to-prepaid** conversions directly into your bank account on your applicable[gateway settlement cycle](https://www.cashfree.com/settlement-and-reconciliation-guide/) , while powering refund payouts through Cashgram. Payout completion depends on successful redemption, available funds and banking systems.
- **Common Reasons for Remittance Delays:** Unresolved NDR exceptions, weight disputes raised by the courier, bank holiday cutoffs, or high RTO deductions offsetting your payable balance.


***Also read:[How to Manage WooCommerce COD Refunds in India](https://www.cashfree.com/blog/manage-woocommerce-cod-refunds-india/)***


### Partial COD Settlement Example


For a ₹2,000 order with ₹200 collected upfront, the courier should collect only the remaining ₹1,800. The ₹200 follows the gateway’s settlement cycle, while the ₹1,800 follows the courier’s COD remittance cycle. Match both receipts to the order and deduct applicable fees when reconciling. If the buyer later pays the balance online, update the courier instruction before delivery.


##


Checklist for Launching Cash on Delivery for Ecommerce


1. **Enable OTP verification** at checkout to verify access to mobile numbers and help reduce fake orders.
2. **Use[Partial COD](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/checkout/cod/configure) or[RTO intelligence](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/checkout/cod/rto)** (via tools like Cashfree One Click Checkout) on high-value or high-return SKUs.
3. **Negotiate your remittance cycle** with your courier or aggregator before scaling ad spend.
4. **Automate COD refunds** with payout links so as to build buyer trust and to facilitate speedy refunds.


##


Conclusion


Cash on delivery remains a trusted growth lever for e-commerce businesses, particularly early stage startups who want to reach Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities or break into new audience segments. FAQs


#### 1. How long does COD settlement take in India?


COD settlement is usually calculated from the date of delivery (D), not the order date. Standard remittance timelines vary by provider, plan, working days and payout cutoffs. Some providers offer Early COD, such as D+1 or D+2, for eligible accounts or an additional fee. Check the agreed remittance schedule before planning cash flow.


#### 2. Does Cashfree collect physical cash at the customer’s doorstep?


No. The logistics partner handles remittance. Cashfree Payments manages the digital layer, verifying buyer contact details at checkout, restricting COD for high-RTO orders, collecting partial COD deposits if configured, and supporting COD-to-prepaid conversions.


#### 3. How can Indian e-commerce businesses reduce COD Return to Origin (RTO) rates?


Businesses can lower RTO rates by using Cashfree One Click Checkout to verify buyers with OTPs, hide COD for high-risk shoppers using AI RTO intelligence,[restrict COD for high-RTO pincodes](https://www.cashfree.com/docs/payments/checkout/cod/blacklist-cod) , require a small Partial COD upfront payment, and use supported prepaid-conversion flows before dispatch. Confirm feature availability for your integration, and update the courier’s collectable amount to prevent double collection.


#### 4. How do COD refunds work when a customer returns a product?


Using **Cashfree Payouts (Cashgram)** , businesses send out a payout link via WhatsApp or SMS to the customer once the refund is approved. The customer simply clicks the link, completes verification, enters their UPI ID or bank details, and receives the refund after successful processing, reducing manual data collection errors. Refund approval, return checks and bank processing still affect the end-to-end timeline.
